content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new loss function and a new architecture of the neural network to balance inter-class and intra-class distances of features and this loss function is used for face forgery detection. Margin penalties in Euclidean and angular space are introduced. The authors show outperforming performance compared with current state-of-the-art works in the experimental results section and claim the effectiveness of the proposed method from the presented results.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper is on a topic of wide interest and attempts to introduce a new loss to balance the feature distributions for the 2-class problem.

However, there are several technical imitations with this paper that are listed in the following: -

A) In Table 3, the comparison is not fair. I suggest the authors add supplementary experiments for fair comparison to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture of the neural network and the proposed loss function, respectively. The models such as Xception and FDFL are different from the model used in this paper, and the loss functions used in Xception and FDFL are also different. The proposed method (new architecture and new loss function) performs better than other methods listed in this table, experiments should be conducted where architecture or new loss function is solely adopted.

B) The authors claim in the methodology section that loss functions such as SphereFace, Arcface, Center loss suffer from poor generalization ability. However, the authors failed to 1) prove the generalization ability and 2) provide comparison with the state-of-the-art loss function that is proposed recently.

C) The authors claim that the proposed loss function has good generalization ability. Therefore, I suggest the authors to apply this proposed loss function to other tasks. For example, the authors can conduct experiments for image classification and compare the proposed loss function with other state-of-the-art methods. Only applying this proposed new loss function on such a narrow topic (face forgery detection) is not adequate to validate such claim.

D) The authors should present persuasive ablation studies to show the effectiveness of the proposed loss function and compare this loss function with SphereFace, Arcface, Center loss and the new Elasticface [1]. However, it is regrettable that we can only see the comparison between softmax loss, softmax + triplet loss etc.

E) In addition, there are several missing citations related to the topic of fake detection. This paper utilizes the information both from RGB and frequency domain for fake detection. However, the authors miss citing other papers which also utilize the RGB/frequency information for fake detection. Here I list several highly related papers [2,3,4,5].

Reference:
[1] Boutros, Fadi, et al. "Elasticface: Elastic margin loss for deep face recognition." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022.
[2] Frank, Joel, et al. "Leveraging frequency analysis for deep fake image recognition." International conference on machine learning. PMLR, 2020.
[3] X. Zhang, S. Karaman and S. -F. Chang, "Detecting and Simulating Artifacts in GAN Fake Images," 2019 IEEE International Workshop on Information Forensics and Security (WIFS), 2019, pp. 1-6, doi: 10.1109/WIFS47025.2019.9035107.
[4] Durall, Ricard, Margret Keuper, and Janis Keuper. "Watch your up-convolution: Cnn based generative deep neural networks are failing to reproduce spectral distributions." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference on computer vision and pattern recognition. 2020.
[5] Dong, Chengdong, Ajay Kumar, and Eryun Liu. "Think Twice Before Detecting GAN-Generated Fake Images From Their Spectral Domain Imprints." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is adequately clear on the motivation (and expectations) for the new loss function.

However, the contributions claimed by authors on page 2 are not experimentally evaluated. Such limitations with the required evaluation are outlined in earlier comments.
content.summary_of_the_review: There are several serious technical problems in this paper, and these are largely related to limited experimentation and comparisons. These are clearly outlined in earlier comments. In absence of these comparisons, it's hard to evaluate the merit of the loss function articulated in this paper. Penalty for the expected distributions from any new loss function should be rigorously evaluated and is a serious limitation of this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors combine angular loss and Euclidean loss to improve deepfake detection. The experimental results show that it is effective.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

Applying the proposed loss on deepfake detection outperforms other state-of-the-art.



Weakness: 
1. The proposed loss is simply combination of two existing losses.
2.  Fig. 1 and text does not match. More clearly, Fig. 1 has a min operator but Leuc in text does not have. In addition, I don’t know what the min operators in Fig. 1 do. Minimizing respect with what? 
3. In Table 3, the hyper-parameters balancing the losses, e.g., softmax+triplet loss can affect the results a lot but the authors do not report how they tune them.
4. Are the differences of the methods, in particular in videos significant?  For FF+, 140 videos are used in tested. The authors do not say clear about Celeb-DF.
5. Justification for using norm x in the angular loss is needed. 
6. For other losses with hyperparameters, the authors should give the details how the hyperparameters are set.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is readable. I can follow the idea and discussion. However, it is full of grammatical errors and typos. In addition, Fig. 1 and the main text do not match. It is unacceptable to me. 

The novelty of this work is very low. It is in fact just combining two existing losses. I suspect whether this novelty is enough for ICRL.

The loss is simple. It should be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Novelty is low.

The presentation quality is not up to the standard.

The proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a novel loss function called concentric ring loss applied in the detection of face forgery. The new loss function explores penalties in the angular and Euclidean space, to enhance intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Particularly, the method explores high-frequency domains to introduce clues for face forgery. The paper presents experiments in the FF++ (Face Forensics++) and Celeb-DF, showing that it outperforms state-fo-the-art methods and also shows a better performance in unseen data, showing good generalisation ability.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1) the paper is well written and motivated
2) the presented method explores frequency domain information to find important cues for detection of manipulated images. It shows that the new concentric ring loss is able to force intra-class compactness and inter-class separability by leveraging the angular and Euclidean space penalties. The whole idea is very reasonable and is comprehensively tested.
3) experimental section is very clear and well organised, showing good results of the method, able to outperform state-of-the-art.

Weaknesses:
1) there are a few typos and the general quality of the text will benefit from being revised
2) it is not clear how fusion of the RGB branch and frequency branch is made. The authors should explain how this fusion is performed.
3) The architecture for feature extraction is not well stabilised. The authors should provide more details on it.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is very clear and well written. 
The novelty of the paper is reasonable by exploring novel ideas, although incremental, ie. the novelty is limited.
For the sake of reproducibility, the authors should make the code available.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is very interesting and a very well organised research method. It can benefit from a text revision and maybe to clarify a few parts of the method.

content.title: Concentric Ring Loss for Face Forgery Detection
content.abstract: Due to growing societal concerns about indistinguishable deepfake images, face forgery detection has received an increasing amount of interest in computer vision. Since the differences between actual and fake images are frequently small, improving the discriminative ability of learnt features is one of the primary problems in deepfake detection. In this paper, we propose a novel Concentric Ring Loss (CRL) to encourage the model to learn intra-class compressed and inter-class separated features. Specifically, we independently add margin penalties in angular and Euclidean space to force a more significant margin between real and fake images, and hence encourage better discriminating performance. Compared to softmax loss, CRL explicitly encourages intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Moreover, a frequency-aware feature learning module is proposed to exploit high-frequency features and further improve the generalization ability of the model. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our methods over different datasets. We show that CRL consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art by a large margin.
